title: Quant Perf Dashboard Mockup + Metric Naming Proposals (FP8/INT8 sprint)
content:
Owner: Allison
Reviewers: Aisha, Sean, Noah, Rina
Last updated: 2025-10-12

Context
- This is a working mockup for the “Quant Perf” dashboard supporting the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint.
- Primary goals:
  (1) let runtime + SRE quickly answer “did perf move?” and “why?” across GPU/model/quant mode/runtime commit
  (2) provide a stable metric/tag vocabulary so benchmark artifacts + runtime spans + canary jobs all join cleanly
  (3) enable regression alerts (nightly canary + ad-hoc runs) without pager fatigue

Non-goals
- This is not the customer-facing usage dashboard. It is internal perf + correctness guardrail visibility for runtime changes.

Quick links
- Metric definitions ADR: confluence://eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/adr-quant-benchmark-metrics-and-definitions
- Quant perf dashboard spec (more formal): confluence://eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/quant-perf-dashboard-spec
- Dashboard panels implementation PR: github://observability-pack/pr_97
- Runtime spans/logging: github://redwood/pr_10621, github://redwood/pr_10631, github://redwood/pr_10632
- Perf canary jobs: github://perf-canary/pr_188, github://perf-canary/pr_189

========================
1) Proposed metric namespaces
========================

We have three “sources of truth” for perf data:
A) Benchmark harness results (batch jobs; discrete runs)
B) Runtime in-situ metrics/spans (serving traffic; continuous)
C) Perf-canary comparator output (nightly; pass/fail + deltas)

Recommendation: use a single top-level namespace “redwood_inference_” and segment by domain.

A) Benchmark harness (perf-lab)
- Prefix: redwood_inference_bench_
- These are emitted by the benchmark runner / results ingester.

B) Runtime serving metrics
- Prefix: redwood_inference_runtime_
- These are emitted by production runtime processes (or by perf-lab runtime with same exporters).

C) Canary comparator
- Prefix: redwood_inference_canary_

If we must align with existing conventions, OK to alias in the dashboard, but we should keep the canonical names stable.


========================
2) Canonical tag set (labels)
========================

This is the critical part. Without consistent labels across bench + runtime + canary, the dashboard becomes a “choose your own adventure.”

Required labels (every quant perf metric should have these if applicable)
- env: "perf-lab" | "staging" | "prod"
- region: e.g. "us-east" | "us-west" | "eu-central" (perf-lab can still use the region value where the lab is)
- gpu_sku: "A100-80GB" | "H100-80GB" | "H200-141GB" | "L40S-48GB" | "MI300X-192GB" (optional)
- node_pool: "perf-lab-a" etc (optional but useful for contention debugging)
- model_family: "llama" | "qwen" | "mistral" (coarse grouping)
- model_id: Redwood model registry id (e.g. "llama-3.1-70b-instruct")
- model_variant: "base" | "instruct" | "chat" (optional; only if we actually use it)
- quant_mode: "fp16" | "bf16" | "fp8" | "int8"
- quant_profile: e.g. "fp8_e4m3_per_tensor" | "int8_w8a8_symmetric" (string; “unknown” if not set)
- runtime_version: semantic-ish version OR build label (e.g. "runtime-1.38.2")
- runtime_commit: git SHA (short ok)
- container_digest: sha256… (perf-lab reproducibility)

Phase/shape labels
- phase: "prefill" | "decode" | "total"
- seq_bucket: standardized buckets for prompt/ctx len and decode len (see below)
- batch_bucket: small set of buckets (1, 2-4, 5-8, 9-16, 17+)

Kernel attribution labels (best-effort; behind runtime flag)
- kernel_family: "flashattn" | "cutlass" | "triton" | "cublaslt" | "custom" | "unknown"
- kernel_id: stable ID from runtime logging (string; can include algo/tile)
- op_name: "attention" | "gemm" | "rmsnorm" | "rope" | "kv_cache" | "unknown" (we may need to align with runtime spans)

Scheduler labels
- scheduler_policy: "default" | "quant_decode_cap" | "prefill_prio" etc
- batch_cap: numeric as string (e.g. "8") or "default"

Notes
- Use model_id as the join key across systems; use model_family for aggregation.
- runtime_commit should always be available in perf-lab (pinned builds). In prod, runtime_version may be more reliable.


========================
3) Bucketing standards
========================

We need a shared bucketing spec so panels are stable.

Sequence buckets (seq_bucket) proposal
- "ctx_0_512"
- "ctx_513_2k"
- "ctx_2k_8k"
- "ctx_8k_32k"
- "ctx_32k_plus"

Decode buckets (decode_bucket) if we need separate
- "gen_0_64"
- "gen_65_256"
- "gen_257_1k"
- "gen_1k_plus"

If we only get one bucket label, we should define it as context length bucket (prompt tokens) because TTFT is more sensitive there.


========================
4) Key metrics (aligned to ADR)
========================

Primary “serving experience” metrics
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) ms
- TPOT (time-per-output-token) ms/token (or tokens/sec; pick one canonical and derive the other)
- E2E latency ms (for non-streaming)

Throughput/cost proxy metrics
- tokens_per_second (decode)
- requests_per_second (where meaningful)
- gpu_seconds_per_1k_tokens (cost proxy; for perf-lab)

Queueing/scheduler metrics
- queue_wait_ms (prefill vs decode)
- batch_size (observed)

Kernel-level contributions (profiling-derived or span-derived)
- op_time_ms by op_name (attention/gemm/kv_cache/etc)
- kernel_launch_count (optional)

Correctness guardrails
- numeric_drift_p50 / p95 (INT8/FP8 vs FP16 reference) for a fixed small prompt set
- fallback_rate (fraction of requests that fell back to fp16/bf16)


========================
5) Proposed concrete metric names
========================

Benchmark harness (histograms preferred)
- redwood_inference_bench_ttft_ms_bucket / _sum / _count
  labels: env, region, gpu_sku, model_id, quant_mode, runtime_commit, phase="prefill", seq_bucket, concurrency, streaming
- redwood_inference_bench_tpot_ms_bucket / _sum / _count
  labels: phase="decode" etc
- redwood_inference_bench_tokens_per_second_gauge
  labels: phase, …
- redwood_inference_bench_gpu_seconds_per_1k_tokens_gauge
  labels: phase, …
- redwood_inference_bench_success_rate_gauge
  labels: error_class maybe

Runtime (serving)
- redwood_inference_runtime_request_latency_ms_bucket
  labels: route, model_id, quant_mode, phase (if phase-level exists), streaming
- redwood_inference_runtime_ttft_ms_bucket
  labels: model_id, quant_mode, scheduler_policy, gpu_sku (if known), region
- redwood_inference_runtime_tpot_ms_bucket
- redwood_inference_runtime_queue_wait_ms_bucket
  labels: phase, scheduler_policy
- redwood_inference_runtime_fallback_total (counter)
  labels: from_quant_mode, to_quant_mode, reason

Kernel attribution (span/log-derived)
- redwood_inference_runtime_op_time_ms_bucket
  labels: op_name, kernel_family, kernel_id, model_id, quant_mode, phase

Canary comparator
- redwood_inference_canary_regression_score_gauge
  labels: metric="ttft"|"tpot"|"tokens_per_second" etc, model_id, gpu_sku, quant_mode
- redwood_inference_canary_delta_pct_gauge
  labels: baseline_runtime_commit, candidate_runtime_commit, metric, …
- redwood_inference_canary_pass_gauge (0/1)
  labels: rule_id, …


========================
6) Dashboard mockup (panels)
========================

Dashboard name
- “Quant Perf: FP8/INT8 (Bench + Canary + Runtime)”

Global filters (top row)
- env (default perf-lab)
- region
- gpu_sku
- model_family
- model_id
- quant_mode (multi-select; default fp8 + int8 + fp16 baseline)
- runtime_commit OR runtime_version
- scheduler_policy
- streaming (true/false)
- concurrency (bench-only)

Panel group A: Release / change detection
A1) Canary status table (last 14 days)
- columns: date, gpu_sku, model_id, quant_mode, metric, delta_pct, pass/fail, link_to_run
- goal: immediate “what broke?”

A2) Delta vs baseline (selected candidate vs baseline)
- TTFT p95 delta (%), TPOT p95 delta (%), tokens/sec delta (%)
- include a “variability band” (p25–p75 across repeats) if available

Panel group B: User-perceived latency (streaming)
B1) TTFT p50/p95 by quant_mode
- breakdown: quant_mode, facet by gpu_sku
- separate row for seq_bucket (ctx buckets)

B2) TPOT p50/p95 by quant_mode
- same structure

B3) Phase timing stacked bar (prefill vs decode)
- Use bench_phase_time_ms or derived from logs

Panel group C: Throughput / cost proxy
C1) tokens/sec (decode) by quant_mode
C2) gpu_seconds_per_1k_tokens by quant_mode
- note: only perf-lab; hide in prod env

Panel group D: Scheduler + queueing
D1) Queue wait p95 by phase (prefill/decode)
- split by scheduler_policy and quant_mode
D2) Observed batch size distribution
- show percentiles and histogram bucket counts

Panel group E: Kernel attribution (only if spans enabled)
E1) Top op_time_ms contributors (p95) (table)
- rows: op_name
- columns: fp16, fp8, int8 (p95), delta
- include kernel_family and kernel_id in drilldown

E2) Kernel selection breakdown (pie / table)
- percent of requests by kernel_family/kernel_id for attention and gemm
- helps catch wrong auto-selection

Panel group F: Guardrails
F1) Fallback rate over time
- if fallback increases, perf might look “stable” but we’re not using quant path

F2) Numeric drift summary
- show p95 drift metric for FP8/INT8 vs FP16 for the standard prompt set


========================
7) Example queries (PromQL-ish placeholders)
========================

NOTE: These are examples for panel wiring; exact metric names may differ after exporter implementation. Assumes histograms.

TTFT p95 (bench)
- histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, model_id, gpu_sku, quant_mode) (
    rate(redwood_inference_bench_ttft_ms_bucket{env="perf-lab", phase="prefill", streaming="true"}[15m])
  ))

TPOT p95 (bench)
- histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, model_id, gpu_sku, quant_mode) (
    rate(redwood_inference_bench_tpot_ms_bucket{env="perf-lab", phase="decode", streaming="true"}[15m])
  ))

Tokens/sec (bench) (if gauge)
- avg by (model_id, gpu_sku, quant_mode) (
    redwood_inference_bench_tokens_per_second_gauge{env="perf-lab", phase="decode"}
  )

Queue wait p95 (runtime)
- histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, phase, quant_mode, scheduler_policy) (
    rate(redwood_inference_runtime_queue_wait_ms_bucket{env="$env"}[10m])
  ))

Fallback rate (runtime)
- sum by (model_id, quant_mode) (
    rate(redwood_inference_runtime_fallback_total{env="$env"}[10m])
  )
  /
  sum by (model_id, quant_mode) (
    rate(redwood_inference_runtime_requests_total{env="$env"}[10m])
  )

Kernel/op contribution p95
- topk(10,
    histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, op_name, kernel_family) (
      rate(redwood_inference_runtime_op_time_ms_bucket{env="$env", model_id="$model"}[10m])
    ))
  )


========================
8) Alerting proposal (internal only)
========================

Routing
- All quant perf alerts -> #eng-runtime (FYI) and #eng-sre (action) depending on severity.
- For sprint: route to #eng-runtime by default; escalate to oncall only if canary indicates multi-GPU + multi-model regression.

Alert types
1) Canary regression fail (page: no; slack: yes)
- Trigger: redwood_inference_canary_pass_gauge == 0 for any “tier-1” model_id+gpu_sku+quant_mode combination
- Add inhibition: if env=perf-lab has known incident ongoing (Sean to provide a flag)

2) Fallback rate spike (slack)
- Trigger: fallback_rate > 2% for >15m in perf-lab; in prod threshold higher / disable until stable

3) Metric missing (slack)
- Trigger: no samples for required metrics for N minutes while job is running (helps catch exporter/schema break)


========================
9) Instrumentation requirements / dependencies
========================

To populate E panels (kernel attribution), we need:
- kernel selection + quant mode tracing spans (github://redwood/pr_10621)
- structured perf log events (github://redwood/pr_10631)
- scheduler instrumentation for queue wait histograms (github://redwood/pr_10632)

Bench harness needs to emit:
- stable metadata tags: gpu_sku, runtime_commit, container_digest, model_id, quant_mode, prompt distribution id
- recommended: results artifact includes histogram buckets so we don’t rely on only p50/p95 point estimates

Open question: where does the join happen?
- Option 1: ingester writes time series directly to TSDB (Prom)
- Option 2: write parquet/json to object store and dashboard reads via data source (Grafana + Athena/Trino)
- For sprint speed: TSDB + lightweight retention may be sufficient; long-term: parquet for deep analysis.


========================
10) Open questions / decisions needed
========================

1) Canonical unit for TPOT
- ms/token vs tokens/sec. I propose canonical = ms/token (lower is better) and derive tokens/sec.
- Reason: aligns with latency SLAs and makes p95 interpretation consistent.

2) runtime_commit label in prod
- Do we have a reliable way to tag runtime_commit in prod metrics? If not, use runtime_version and keep commit only in perf-lab.

3) GPU SKU label in runtime metrics
- In prod, sometimes the process doesn’t know the exact SKU (esp. abstracted environments). If missing, use instance_type or accelerator_type.

4) seq_bucket generation
- Do we bucket at request time (runtime) or at benchmark config (harness)? Prefer runtime-side for accuracy.

5) Kernel IDs stability
- We should treat kernel_id as a debug label only. For aggregate dashboards, kernel_family is safer to avoid cardinality blowups.


========================
11) Next steps (owners)
========================

- [Allison] Align metric names with quant-perf-dashboard-spec and implement Grafana panels (tracked in github://observability-pack/pr_97).
- [Aisha] Define alert rules + routing + “known perf-lab incident” inhibition flag.
- [Julian] Confirm scheduler queue wait histogram label set matches proposed tags (phase, quant_mode, scheduler_policy).
- [Rina] Confirm benchmark ingester can emit required labels (runtime_commit, container_digest, seq_bucket).
- [Noah] Sanity-check that TTFT/TPOT aggregation matches ADR and that we’re not mixing streaming and non-streaming runs.
